title: Listening Comprehension
intro: Listen to a dialogue, then answer multiple choice questions. Many answers are spread across several turns, so keep track of numbers, days, times, and places, and listen for reasons, feelings, what a phrase means, and what the speakers will do next. These are generated review dialogues on Module 2 topics (Airborn, The Secret Garden, The Miracle of Spring, The Poem That Will Not End), because the midterm dialogue is only played in class.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Owen, you froze again in scene three. You were supposed to say, "The garden is awake!" and you just stood there.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: I know. When everyone is watching, I panic and the words disappear. Last night I remembered the line perfectly in my bedroom.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The stage directions say you hesitate at the gate for two seconds, then you seize the key and push the door open. Maybe you are hesitating too long.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Two seconds feels like forever up there. And the vines on the gate keep catching my sleeve. Today a tendril wrapped right around my button.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That is a costume problem, not an acting problem. I will ask Ms. Lopez to fix the fastening on your jacket so nothing catches.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Thanks. But what if I forget the line on Friday night, in front of a hundred parents?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Then look at Lily. She is playing the robin, and she sits right beside the gate. She can whisper the first word to you.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Lily is so restless during long scenes. She is always fidgeting with her feathers. I don't think she would even notice.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Then let's make it easier. We are rehearsing again on Thursday at three thirty. Bring your script, and we will run scene three five times in a row.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Five times? I guess that is reasonable. Today I attempted it only once before I gave up.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Exactly. And remember, Colin is supposed to feel amazed, not scared. If you act amazed, the line will come out naturally.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Amazed, not scared. Okay. Tonight I will practice in front of my little brother. He is a tough audience.

questions.q: Why does Owen freeze in scene three?
choices: He never learned the line at home.
Lily whispered the wrong word to him.
He panics when everyone is watching him.
The gate is locked and he cannot open it.

questions.q: According to the stage directions, what should Owen do at the gate?
choices: Hesitate for two seconds, then seize the key and push the door open
Seize the key right away and run into the garden
Wait for the robin to whisper the first word
Hesitate for five seconds, then say his line

questions.q: What problem does the tendril cause, and how will it be solved?
choices: It blocks the gate, so Mia will cut the vine.
It covers the key, so Lily will hold the vine back.
It makes Owen trip, so he will wear different shoes.
It catches on Owen's button, so Ms. Lopez will fix the fastening on his jacket.

questions.q: Why doesn't Owen want to depend on Lily?
choices: She does not know his line.
She is restless and might not notice he needs help.
She sits too far away from the gate.
She is not coming to the show on Friday.

questions.q: When will Owen perform the play in front of the parents?
choices: Thursday at three thirty
Tonight, at home
Friday night
Next Thursday

questions.q: What advice does Mia give Owen about acting the scene?
choices: Act amazed instead of scared, and the line will come naturally.
Skip the line if he forgets it.
Hesitate longer so the audience feels nervous.
Read the line from his script on stage.

questions.q: When Owen calls his little brother "a tough audience," what does he mean?
choices: His brother is very strong.
His brother will be in the play too.
His brother loves every show he watches.
His brother is hard to impress.

questions.q: What will Owen do tonight?
choices: Run scene three five times with Mia
Practice his line in front of his little brother
Ask Ms. Lopez to fix his jacket
Write a new line for Colin

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: Ethan, Mr. Brooks wants our watering schedule by Monday. Have you looked at the seed packets yet?

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: I am reading them right now. The peas say to plant them densely, about two inches apart, and the carrots need full sun.

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: The sunniest bed is the one by the fence. But last spring the tomatoes there turned yellow.

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: Mr. Brooks said that was a deficiency in the soil. It was missing nutrients, so on Tuesday our class mixed in compost.

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: Good. So, peas by the fence? Their tendrils can climb up the fence wires.

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: Perfect. Then the carrots go in the middle bed. Now the hard part: who waters during spring break?

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: Not me. My family is flying to my grandma's house for the whole week. We are leaving on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: I am staying home, but I can only come on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. My soccer camp is on the other days.

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: The packet says the seeds need water every day until they sprout. Three days a week is not enough unless the weather is favorable.

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: The forecast says rain on Tuesday and Thursday. That covers two more days. But what about the weekend?

lines.speaker: Zoe
lines.text: Ask Priya. She lives across the street from school, and she told me she wanted a project for the break.

lines.speaker: Ethan
lines.text: Great idea. I will text her tonight. Then we can write the schedule together and give it to Mr. Brooks on Monday.

questions.q: Where will the peas be planted, and why?
choices: In the middle bed, because they need full sun
By the fence, because their tendrils can climb the wires
Across the street, because Priya can water them
By the fence, because the tomatoes grew well there

questions.q: Why did the tomatoes turn yellow last spring?
choices: They did not get enough rain.
They were planted too densely.
The soil had a deficiency and was missing nutrients.
The fence blocked the sunlight.

questions.q: What did the class do on Tuesday?
choices: They mixed compost into the soil.
They planted the carrots.
They watered the seeds.
They gave the schedule to Mr. Brooks.

questions.q: Why can't Zoe water the garden during spring break?
choices: She has soccer camp every day.
She lives too far from school.
She has to write the schedule.
She is flying to her grandma's house for the whole week.

questions.q: On which days can Ethan water the garden?
choices: Tuesday and Thursday
Saturday and Sunday
Monday, Wednesday, and Friday
Every day of the week

questions.q: How do the speakers expect the seeds to get water on Tuesday and Thursday?
choices: Rain is in the forecast for those days.
Mr. Brooks will water them.
Zoe will come back early.
Ethan will skip soccer camp.

questions.q: In this conversation, "favorable" weather means weather that
choices: is cold and windy
helps the plants, such as rain
is sunny every single day
stops the children from coming to school

questions.q: Why do Zoe and Ethan think Priya can water on the weekend?
choices: She is in Mr. Brooks's class.
She has soccer camp with Ethan.
She planted the carrots.
She lives across the street from school and wants a project.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Dad, look! This is a real airship cabin. You can look through the porthole and see a painted sky that moves.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: It is wonderful. But the museum closes at five, and we only have forty minutes left, so we need to choose carefully.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: I want to see everything! The sign says a guide is presiding over a flight demonstration at four thirty in Hall B.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: And you also wanted to see the mysterious logbook, right? The one the captain scrawled in during the storm.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Yes! A worker said the captain wrote it while the ship was shaking, so the words are messy. People still argue about what the last page says.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: The logbook is upstairs in Hall D, and the line was long when we walked by. About twenty people were waiting.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: If we wait in that line, we will miss the demonstration. I can't decide. I am hesitating like a character in a story.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Here is a reasonable plan. The demonstration only lasts fifteen minutes. We watch it first, then go upstairs. The line will probably be shorter by then.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: But what if Hall D closes before we get there?

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Then we buy the book about the logbook in the gift shop. It has photos of every page, so you can try to read the scrawl at home.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Deal. I will bring my notebook to the demonstration and write down how the engines work. Mr. Diaz said we should witness something real for our report.

lines.speaker: Dad
lines.text: Good thinking. Let's go. Hall B is to the left, past the hot-air balloon.

questions.q: About what time is it at the start of the conversation?
choices: Four thirty
Four twenty
Four forty-five
Five o'clock

questions.q: Where is the mysterious logbook?
choices: In the airship cabin
In Hall B, next to the demonstration
Upstairs in Hall D
In the gift shop, past the hot-air balloon

questions.q: Why is the captain's logbook hard to read?
choices: He wrote it while the ship was shaking in a storm.
The pages were torn by the wind.
It is written in another language.
It is kept behind a dark porthole.

questions.q: What does Nora mean when she says, "I am hesitating like a character in a story"?
choices: She wants to act in a play.
She is reading a story about an airship.
She is afraid of the airship cabin.
She cannot make up her mind about what to do.

questions.q: Why does Dad suggest watching the demonstration first?
choices: Because Hall D is already closed
Because it is short and the logbook line will probably be shorter later
Because the logbook is not very interesting
Because the gift shop closes at four thirty

questions.q: If they follow Dad's plan, at about what time will the demonstration end?
choices: Four forty-five
Four thirty
Five o'clock
Five fifteen

questions.q: What will they do if Hall D closes before they get there?
choices: Come back to the museum tomorrow
Ask the guide to read the last page
Look through the porthole again
Buy the book with photos of every logbook page

questions.q: Why will Nora bring her notebook to the demonstration?
choices: To copy the words in the logbook
To draw the painted sky
To write down how the engines work for her report
To get the guide's autograph

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Jack, did you finish your poem for the spring poetry contest? The deadline is Wednesday at noon.

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: I finished it last night! I was so happy I felt almost delirious. But my sister read it with contempt and called it a silly ditty.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Don't listen to her. What is it about?

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: It is about a seed that awakens in spring. Every stanza ends with the same refrain: "Wake up, little seed, the sun is here."

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: I love that refrain. It sounds like a song. How long is the poem?

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: Thirty-two lines. I kept adding stanzas: a worm, a robin, a rain cloud. It is like the poem that will not end.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Uh-oh. The rules say twenty lines or fewer. The judges will not even read a poem that is too long.

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: Twenty? Then I have to cut twelve lines. Which ones should go?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Keep the refrain, because it is the best part. Maybe cut the worm and the rain cloud. The robin stanza is the funniest.

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: But the rain cloud stanza took me a whole hour to write. I really don't want to delete it.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Then save it in your notebook for another poem. A poem is like a garden. Sometimes you pull a few plants so the others can grow.

lines.speaker: Jack
lines.text: Okay, okay. I will cut the worm and the rain cloud tonight, read the new version to you tomorrow at lunch, and hand it in on Wednesday morning.

questions.q: When is the deadline for the poetry contest?
choices: Tomorrow at lunch
Wednesday at noon
Wednesday morning
Tonight

questions.q: How did Jack's sister react to his poem?
choices: She treated it with contempt and called it a silly ditty.
She was delirious with joy.
She helped him add a stanza about a robin.
She told him to enter the contest.

questions.q: When Jack says he felt "almost delirious," he means he felt
choices: sick and tired
angry at his sister
wildly excited
worried about the deadline

questions.q: What is the refrain of Jack's poem?
choices: "The garden is awake!"
"Rain cloud, rain cloud, bring the spring."
"Little robin, sing to me."
"Wake up, little seed, the sun is here."

questions.q: Why does Jack have to make his poem shorter?
choices: The judges will not read poems longer than twenty lines.
His sister said it was boring.
Emma does not like the refrain.
He has to read it aloud in one minute.

questions.q: How many lines must Jack cut?
choices: Twenty
Thirty-two
Two
Twelve

questions.q: What does Emma mean when she says, "A poem is like a garden"?
choices: Jack should write a poem about vegetables.
Removing some parts can help the best parts stand out.
Poems grow bigger every spring.
Jack should read his poem outside.

questions.q: What will Jack do tomorrow at lunch?
choices: Hand in his poem to the judges
Write a new stanza about a worm
Read the shorter version of his poem to Emma
Show the rain cloud stanza to his sister

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Max, why do you look so worried? And why are you carrying that big cardboard box?

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: I made a terrible mistake at the school auction. I only raised my hand to wave at you, and now I own box number nine.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Box nine? That is the mystery box! Nobody knows its contents. How much did it cost?

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: Eighteen dollars. The man presiding over the auction pointed at me and shouted, "Sold!" before I could explain.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Didn't you try to stop him?

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: I attempted to, but everyone was clapping so loudly. My mom was busy restraining my little sister, who was jumping up and down.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Well, all the money goes to the school library, so it is not wasted. Let's open it. Something is rattling inside.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: Okay. There is a matted old teddy bear, a brass key, and a folded map.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: A key and a map? This is just like The Secret Garden! Maybe the key opens something hidden.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: The map shows our school field. There is an X next to the old oak tree, and someone scrawled "Spring 1996" at the bottom.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: That was thirty years ago! Maybe a class buried a time capsule. We should show Principal Lee before we dig anywhere.

lines.speaker: Max
lines.text: You are right. The groundskeeper is very watchful about that field, and we would be in big trouble. Principal Lee is at the bake sale table until three o'clock.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: It is two forty-five now. If we hurry, we can catch her. You bring the key, and I will carry the map.

questions.q: How did Max end up buying box number nine?
choices: He wanted the teddy bear inside it.
His little sister raised her hand for him.
He raised his hand to wave at Sophie, and the man thought he was bidding.
Sophie asked him to buy it for the library.

questions.q: How much did Max pay for the box?
choices: Eighteen dollars
Nine dollars
Thirty dollars
Fifteen dollars

questions.q: Why couldn't Max stop the auction in time?
choices: His mom told him to stay quiet.
Everyone was clapping loudly, and his mom was busy with his sister.
The man presiding over the auction had already left.
Sophie was waving at him.

questions.q: Why does Sophie say the money is "not wasted"?
choices: Because the box has a valuable key
Because Max can sell the teddy bear
Because the box was cheaper than the others
Because the money goes to the school library

questions.q: Which item was NOT in the box?
choices: A matted teddy bear
A brass key
A shovel
A folded map

questions.q: Why does Sophie think a class may have buried a time capsule?
choices: The map has an X by the oak tree and the words "Spring 1996."
The groundskeeper told her about it.
Principal Lee mentioned it at the bake sale.
The teddy bear has a note sewn inside it.

questions.q: Why don't Max and Sophie start digging right away?
choices: They do not have a shovel.
The field is closed for spring break.
The map is too hard to read.
They might get in trouble, so they want to ask Principal Lee first.

questions.q: How much time do they have to find Principal Lee at the bake sale?
choices: Thirty minutes
About fifteen minutes
Forty-five minutes
One hour
